summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a homeless man with chronic systolic heart failure, atrial fibrillation, and alcohol use disorder, was admitted after a syncopal episode with a fall. He reported dizziness and a sensation of spinning, especially when tilting his head back. Evaluation revealed benign paroxysmal positional vertigo (BPPV), confirmed by positional nystagmus, and successfully treated with the Epley maneuver. His implantable cardiac defibrillator was interrogated and found to be functioning properly without recent firing. His heart failure was stable, though an echocardiogram showed reduced ejection fraction at 15%. He developed mild pulmonary edema after holding Lasix, but symptoms resolved with reinstitution of diuretic therapy. His pulmonary embolism was improving, and he remained compliant with Lovenox. No medication changes were made, though spironolactone was recommended for outpatient consideration. He was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to monitor weight, continue all medications, and perform Epley maneuvers as needed.
